_comment: Config for the kanban-cycle skill, read at the start of every cycle. To reuse this automation on another project: copy the .claude/skills/kanban-cycle folder there and write a new file like this one pointing at that project's repo/board.
_comment_cost_ceiling: orchestrator_cost_ceiling_usd thresholds get_session's external_metadata.usage.cost_usd, which values the session's tokens at API list prices. On a subscription plan that is NOT a bill — it is just a convenient running total of token volume, and the real constraint is the rate-limit window (see rate_limit_info in the same response). Tune this by how long you want one orchestrator generation to live, not by a spend budget.
_comment_orchestrator_branch: The branch carrying the current .claude/skills. A new session clones the repo's DEFAULT branch unless told otherwise, so /handoff must check this out explicitly or the successor comes up without the skills that define its own job. Fixed to main at generation 4's handoff (2026-08-31), 3 generations after this was first flagged wrong — main now carries the current skill files (verified via git ls-tree before making this change). If this ever needs to point elsewhere again, that's a regression to investigate, not a new normal.
_comment_maintenance_automerge_paths: Vinnie's standing instruction, 2026-09-03: a maintenance PR (no linked Notion ticket) whose entire diff falls within these paths may merge on green CI alone, without waiting for his review/lgtm first — see kanban-cycle SKILL.md step 3. Deliberately narrow: the orchestrator's own skill/config files only, never app code, migrations, or anything that changes runtime behavior. Widening this list is a decision for Vinnie to make explicitly, not one for a cycle to infer.
_comment_dashboard: The live status board every cycle writes to (kanban-cycle SKILL.md step 7a). It is a published Artifact with the `db` capability: the page holds no state of its own, it renders whatever the orchestrator last wrote to the artifact's document store, so a cycle refreshes it with ONE `write_db` batch (~500 tokens) instead of republishing HTML. The URL is the identity of the board — it survives handoffs, so a successor generation writes to this same URL and Vinnie's bookmark keeps working. Never publish a new artifact for this; that would strand the board Vinnie actually has open. `state/snapshot` is the whole current picture (one document, replaced each cycle). `cycles/<id>` is one short document per cycle, kept to the most recent `cycle_log_keep`. `answers/<needs_you id>` is written by the PAGE, not by a cycle — that is Vinnie replying to a question without opening the session, and step 0 reads it.
_comment_project_key: This project's key on the shared dashboard. Every project writes to the SAME dashboard_artifact_url and owns exactly the documents keyed by its own project_key (`state/<key>`, and the queue entries tagged with it). That is what makes one page answer 'what needs me across everything' instead of one bookmark per project. Must be unique across projects; changing it orphans this project's history on the board.
_comment_externally_owned_ticket_ids: Standing exclusion relayed to generation 8 (2026-09-04) from Vinnie via another session ('PR video mocking with test services', session_011cBxF8xkMUZWyYoJGQpBJC), which he gave these two tickets to own and drive end to end, outside this orchestrator's normal flow. Verified against primary sources before trusting it: the H-8 Notion card carries extensive, dated, internally-consistent decisions attributed to Vinnie that this orchestrator did not write, and the named session is real and active on this same repo. Do not dispatch these tickets, do not triage/rebase/comment/dispatch onto their PRs once opened (two sessions pushing one branch fight each other), and do not count their PRs toward max_open_prs/max_stacked_prs. This is temporary and ticket-specific, not a policy change — remove an ID from this list only when Vinnie says the exclusion is over, never on inference (e.g. the other session going quiet, or its PR merging, isn't by itself proof the exclusion lifted).
